candidate.title: CAGE
candidate.scope: Architecture of the assigned CAGE row, interpreted as the random-primed, cap-trapper, EcoP15I tag implementation supported by Takahashi et al. (2012). Inventory of this row: RNA/Cap overview describing initiation sites of capped coding and noncoding RNAs; Capped mRNA with AA(A)n; N15 random primer with rendered EcoP151 site; Reverse transcription; Biotinylate; upper incomplete and lower cap-reaching hybrid examples; RNase digestion; Capture only complete 5′ ends with upper product faded and lower product retained; Purify cDNA; Add linker and digest wth EcoP151; cDNA endpoint. Arrows connect this route; the two molecular fates are neither independent samples nor alternative target methods. The card title and matching collection page identify CAGE alone. The visible PRO-cap row above, DeepCAGE row below, clipped neighbouring-row labels at the top, and right-hand 3′ terminal-structure chemistry panel are adjacent poster context, with no connecting route into this CAGE row. They do not add targets or operations. This extraction is a schematic architecture, not a complete protocol, and makes no claim that all CAGE-family implementations use this primer or restriction enzyme.

states.label: Linker-processed 5′-end cDNA tags; final schematic cDNA product
features: Final endpoint is the blue line labelled cDNA. The preceding multicolour line and combined caption indicate linker addition and restriction processing.

The matched EcoP15I implementation prepares tags containing the initial 27 nt of capped RNA, together with DNA linker sequences for the sequencing interface; these are not full-transcript RNA molecules.
